clue.text: Move with speed? Have caution and a bit of hesitation

parts.note: caution means care, as in 'handle with care'
er is the little sound of hesitation a speaker makes

explanation.surface: Advice to go carefully, with a pause or two, rather than rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls towards slowness while the definition is about rushing: to career is to charge along at full tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle along fast and often out of control.

clue.text: Phones everybody in the civil service

indicators.note: in tells us the word for everybody sits inside the abbreviation for the civil service

parts.note: CS is the standard abbreviation for the Civil Service
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Every government official is on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phones as a verb means rings up, makes telephone calls to someone.

clue.text: Cockney festival with hidden aim

indicators.note: hidden says the word for aim is tucked away inside the festival's name

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival
an end is a goal or aim, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A Cockney celebration that has a secret purpose behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner from the East End, so an East Ender.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneys traditionally come from the East End of London, so a Cockney is an inhabitant of that district.

clue.text: Thoughtfulness shown by a minority of Yorkshire spectators

indicators.note: a minority of says only a small run of letters is taken from inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Fans at a Yorkshire ground show consideration, though only a few of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the last two letters of 'Yorkshire' and the first five of 'spectators'.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing regard and consideration for others' feelings is a form of thoughtfulness.

clue.text: A tonic possibly right for swallowing, cold drug

indicators.note: for swallowing means the rearranged letters take in the letter for right
possibly hints that the letters of 'A tonic' might be arranged some other way

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up drink, a dash of something right, and a chilly drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A TONIC as NACOTI, which then swallows R after NA; C (cold) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug, especially an opiate, that dulls the senses or induces sleep.

clue.text: A gaol internally repurposed as a building for works of art

definitions.text: a building for works of art

indicators.note: repurposed suggests the letters of the three words are put to a different use, rearranged

explanation.surface: An old prison converted inside into an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' looks like a hint to take inside letters, but it is simply part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Gallery in London's Trafalgar Square houses the UK's collection of Western paintings.

clue.text: Man's dispute over territory

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel or dispute
land means territory, as in a country's lands

explanation.surface: A fellow arguing over a stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' simply links the two pieces; the definition is a man's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowland is a male first name, as in the Victorian postal reformer Rowland Hill.

clue.text: I am drowned by awful blast from drums

indicators.note: drowned by means the contraction for I am is submerged within the jumbled letters
awful suggests the letters of 'blast' come out badly jumbled

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed by a terrible noise coming from the percussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful blast' reads as a din from the drums; 'awful' actually scrambles the word into TBALS, and 'drowned by' sinks the contraction just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbals is an old word for kettledrums, the same instruments as timpani.

clue.text: Happy prisoner in temporary accommodation?

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
tented means covered with or lodged under tents, a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Is a jailbird cheerful while housed in makeshift quarters?
explanation.definitionFit: Being contented means being satisfied and at ease, which is a happy state.

clue.text: Girls in specs? Not good!

indicators.note: Not tells us to leave out the letter for good from the word for specs

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses

explanation.surface: Young women wearing spectacles, and a verdict that this is a bad look.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasses is the Scottish and northern English word for young women.

clue.text: Urban dweller has slave after short time

indicators.note: after places the words for 'has slave' following the letter for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
owns means has, possesses
a man can mean a servant or attendant, as in 'my man'

explanation.surface: A city resident acquired a servant only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A townsman is someone living in a town or city rather than the countryside.

clue.text: See group dynamic developing unconscious mechanism

indicators.note: dynamic implies movement and change, so these letters shift about

explanation.surface: A therapist watches how a group's interactions develop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group dynamic' reads as a psychology phrase, which neatly hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freud's model of the mind, this is the partly unconscious part that acts as conscience.

clue.text: A female — feeble or on fire?

parts.note: lame means weak or feeble, as in a lame excuse

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman is weak or passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame means burning, ablaze.

clue.text: Monitor army coming round to put paid to feud

indicators.note: coming round means the first two words' letters surround the word for finish off

parts.note: to vet is to check or monitor
to put paid to something is to end it
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrive under supervision to stop a long-running quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' puts the word for finishing off inside the other two pieces, just after the first letter. The TA, or Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a bitter, prolonged quarrel, often a blood feud between families.

clue.text: Woman beginning to cry 'I love America!' — and it's true

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

indicators.note: beginning to says to take just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A woman cheerfully professes her love of America, and means it.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracious means truthful, speaking or conveying the truth.

clue.text: Pole about to join clique in the county

indicators.note: about means the word for pole is turned round

parts.note: a rod is a pole, a long thin stick
a set is a social group or clique

explanation.surface: A Polish man is about to join an exclusive circle in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' at the start of the clue is capitalised to suggest a Polish person; it is a rod. DORSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on England's south coast.

clue.text: Duo nearly wrecked song

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the letters of the two words are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of performers nearly ruined their number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' looks as if it trims a word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short simple song with a refrain, or a ring dance.

clue.text: Mister hugged by Dora, terrible disciplinarian

indicators.note: hugged by means the abbreviation is held inside the scrambled name
terrible hints that the letters of the name are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A man embraced by a woman called Dora who is a dreadful martinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' looks like a judgement on Dora, but it rearranges her name as RAOD, and 'hugged by' sets the title between its halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is a strict, unbending person who enforces rules, from the rod used to pack a gun barrel.

clue.text: Skill needed to intercept explosive woman

indicators.note: to intercept means the word for skill cuts into the explosive

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Expertise is required to stop a volatile lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive woman' reads as a fiery person; 'explosive' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Martine is a female first name, the French feminine of Martin.

clue.text: Nobody was such a writer

parts.note: a nod to the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, whose hero Charles Pooter keeps a daily journal

explanation.surface: A dismissal of an author nobody had heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' is the title character of the Grossmiths' 1892 comic novel, not a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Pooter, the 'Nobody', records his days in a journal, making him a keeper of a daily record.

clue.text: Magnificent setting for a duke university student about to collect degree

indicators.note: setting for means the word for magnificent forms a mount around the following letters, as a ring holds a jewel

parts.note: grand means magnificent, splendid

explanation.surface: A splendid occasion for a nobleman at college, before he graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduand is someone who has finished a course and is about to be awarded a degree.

clue.text: Not many turning out to be the opposite

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters are turned around into a new form

explanation.surface: Few people prove to be contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning to another, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Criminal pinching gold article — a bright ring

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the word for criminal grips the heraldic gold

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
or is the heraldic word for gold
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A crook steals a gold item, a gleaming band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like stealing in the surface but means squeezing round. OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a circle of light round the sun or moon, a luminous halo.

clue.text: Makes deflated, literally or figuratively

parts.note: the literal reading is letting the air out of a tyre or balloon; the figurative one is disappointing someone

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase covers both senses: releasing the air from something, and leaving a person crestfallen.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate a tyre is to release its air; to deflate a person is to disappoint them, failing their hopes.

clue.text: Woman in new York is someone who'll look after the kids

definitions.text: someone who'll look after the kids

indicators.note: in shows the woman's name sits inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: Y is short for York, as in NY for New York
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lady in New York works as a childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new York' with a small n looks like the city; N and Y are separate pieces either side of ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a woman employed to care for children in their own home.

clue.text: Leaving out nothing at the start of letter

indicators.note: at the start of places the zero before the word for a letter

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a missive is a letter, especially a long or formal one

explanation.surface: A letter that begins with nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Omissive is an adjective meaning failing to include or omitting.

clue.text: Captain with cricket trousers only half on

indicators.note: only half means just the back half of the word for cricket trousers is kept

parts.note: flannels are the white woollen trousers worn for cricket
on is taken as written

explanation.surface: A team skipper with his whites only pulled up halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half of FLANNELS (the white trousers worn at cricket) is kept, leaving NELS. Horatio Nelson was a naval captain before becoming an admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson commanded ships as a captain before his fame as an admiral at Trafalgar.

clue.text: New hat style could be secret

indicators.note: New suggests the letters of 'hat style' are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh design of headwear might be kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective for the hat, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means furtive or done quietly so as not to be noticed, hence covert.

clue.text: Time for a special dance? Help!

explanation.surface: Someone calls for assistance in the middle of a festive jig.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of May is when maypole dancing traditionally takes place; the radio distress call is the second sense.
